knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A data frame, matrix, or SummarizedExperiment object with abundance measurements (features on rows, replicates/samples on columns) ;; pSamplepairs=Threshold value (c_s) to assign a feature for a replicate sample pair to be reproducible (default is 0.75) ;; pFeatures=Threshold value (c_m) to assign a sample pair for a feature to be reproducible (default is 0.75) ;; alpha=Level of significance to control the False Discovery Rate (FDR), default is 0.05 ;; by=Filtering target in MarrFilterData(), which can be "features", "samplePairs", or "both"
- alternatives: IDR (Irreproducible Discovery Rate) by Li et al. (2011) for measuring reproducibility of high-throughput experiments
- when_to_use: Use when you need to assess and filter high-throughput biological replicate experiments (such as MS-Metabolomics or transcriptomics) to identify consistent (reproducible) and inconsistent (irreproducible) features or sample pairs without relying on parametric assumptions.
- pitfalls: Input data must be preprocessed (filtered for high missingness, imputed, and normalized) before running Marr(). The package expects features on the rows and replicates/samples on the columns.

workflows.name: maximum_rank_reproducibility_analysis
workflows.intent: Assess reproducibility of high-dimensional biological features and sample pairs, visualize the distributions, and filter the dataset.
input: abundance_matrix.csv (a matrix, data frame, or SummarizedExperiment of abundance measurements with features as rows and replicate samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Compute maximum rank reproducibility using Marr() ;; 2. Extract reproducible features and sample pairs using MarrFeatures() and MarrSamplepairs() ;; 3. Check the percentage of reproducible features and sample pairs using MarrFeaturesfiltered() and MarrSamplepairsfiltered() ;; 4. Plot the distributions using MarrPlotSamplepairs() and MarrPlotFeatures() ;; 5. Filter the dataset by features, sample pairs, or both using MarrFilterData()
workflows.code:
library(marr)
Marr_output<- Marr(msprepCOPD, pSamplepairs =
                   0.75, pFeatures = 0.75, alpha=0.05)
Marr_output
head(MarrFeatures(Marr_output))
head(MarrSamplepairs(Marr_output))
MarrFeaturesfiltered(Marr_output)
MarrSamplepairsfiltered(Marr_output)
MarrPlotSamplepairs(Marr_output) 
MarrPlotFeatures(Marr_output) 
MarrFilterData(Marr_output, by = "features")
MarrFilterData(Marr_output, by = "samplePairs")
MarrFilterData(Marr_output, by = "both")
